full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant-petitioner was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the order No.66 dated 28-8-91 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong Sadar in Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 6. On 22-3-1987 said SCC Suit was fixed for hearing and the defendant-petitioner failed to appear in the hearing of the suit, for which it was decreed ex parte on 22-3-87 On 1-4-87 the defendant-petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.136 of 1987 under Section 17 of the Small Cause Courts Act for setting aside the ex parte decree and for restoration of the said suit in its original file and number. 

 7. The said Miscellaneous case was fixed for hearing on 2-8-90 and 2-8-90 being Government holiday, the file was put up for hearing on 4-8-90 and the defendant-petitioner having been found absent said Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 1987 was dismissed for default on 4-8-90. 

 8. On 24-10-90 the defendant-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 under section 17(1) of the SCC Act for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case No.136 of 1987 in its original number and file after vacating the order No. 54 dated 4-8-90. 

 9. The plaintiff opposite parties filed written objection in Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 stating that the Miscellaneous Case is not maintainable under section 17(1) of the SCC Act and that the defendant-petitioner willingly defaulted in appearing in the Court on 4-8-90 for which the Miscellaneous Case No.136 of 1987 was legally dismissed and that the present case is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990 was fixed for hearing on 28-8-91 and the learned Court after hearing the parties rejected the said Miscellaneous Case holding that the case is not maintainable under section 17(1) of the SCC as the order dated 4-8-90 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 1987 being not a decree the provision of section 17(1) of the SC Act is not applicable and the learned trial Court further held that the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable. The learned Court did not give any finding as to the merit of the application for restoration in Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990. 

 12. Mr Faridul Alam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner, has taken me through the revisional application, annexures and the impugned order and submitted that the learned SCC Court committed an error of law in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990 holding that section 17 of the SCC Act is not applicable. He further submitted that the learned SCC Court did not apply his judicial mind in the facts and circumstance of the present case in rejecting the Miscellaneous case. According to the learned Advocate, the provision of section 17 of the SCC Act is also applicable for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990. 

 14. It appears that Abdul Mannaf Contractor as plaintiff filed SCC Suit No.155 of 1985 for ejectment of the defendant-petitioner which was decreed ex parte on 23-3-87. If further appears that the defendant petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 1987 under section 17 of the SCC Act which was also dismissed for default on 14-8- 90. It is admitted that for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No.136 of 1987 the defendant petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990 under section 17(1) of the SCC Act. Now the question is whether this Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 is maintainable under section 17 of the SCC Act or under the General Provision of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 15. A plain reading of the aforesaid section 17 of the SCC Act shows that this section 17 is applicable only for setting aside a decree passed ex parte or for a review of the judgment on condition of deposit in Court the due from the defendant. Here the present Miscellaneous Case No.493 of 1990 was filed challenging the order dated 4-8-90 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 1987 under section 17 of the SCC Act. The order dated 4-8-90 passed in Miscellaneous case No. 136 of 1987 is not a decree but an order rejecting a Miscellaneous Case for restoration of SCC Suit No.155 of 1985. 

 16. In my opinion, the learned SCC Judge rightly held that the application under section 17 of the SCC Act for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No. 136 of 1987 is not maintainable. In the case of Roy Charan Das vs Santosli Kumar Das and others reported in 22 DLR 790 wherein the plaintiffs suit being SCC Suit No.9 of 1968 was dismissed for default, thereafter the plaintiff filed an application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order of dismissal and for restoration of the suit which was ultimately allowed by the SCC Judge and the High Court Division in that decision held that when a SCC Suit is dismissed for default provision of Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable. Having regard to the provision of section 17 of the SCC Act as well as the principle enunciated in the aforesaid decision I am of opinion that the learned trial Court (SCC Judge) committed no error of law in holding that the Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 under section 17(1) of the SCC Act is not maintainable and consequently in rejecting the said Miscellaneous case. 

 For the reasons stated above, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the order dated 28-8-91 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 493 of 1990 is affirmed.
